card.title: NIGHT BOMBING
card.text: Destroy target undamaged unit, then randomly rearrange enemy units on the battlefield.
card.flavorText: The US air force did conduct night bombing missions during WWII, but their focus was primarily on daylight precision bombing. The US Army Air Forces (USAAF) believed that daylight bombing allowed for greater accuracy and minimized the risk of friendly fire incidents. But as the war progressed, the USAAF recognized the need for night bombing capabilities to intensify the strategic bombing campaign against Germany. Therefore in 1943, the USAAF began conducting limited night bombing operations using B-17 Flying Fortress and B-24 Liberator bombers equipped with radar and improved navigational aids. However, it's important to note that night bombing remained a secondary aspect of the USAAF's overall bombing strategy, with daylight precision bombing missions continuing to be the primary focus.
